key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly screen multilayer perovskite solar cells and identify high-efficiency, lead-free architectures without exhaustive simulation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable design strategy for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations in next-generation photovoltaic devices.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device stacks with SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen architectures.
Used SHAP to rank the most influential material descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong rank-correlation performance, and the model predicted top devices later confirmed by SCAPS-1D, including FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the representativeness of the simulated training set, so transfer to new materials or fabrication conditions may require recalibration.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
